newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields dive, to rally into budget.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields dive, to rally into budget.

text.p: *Long dated Australian bond yields dropped to the lowest level since late February, prompted by shortcovering following an unusally marked move in U.S. debt on comments by Greenspan.
*Market seen rallying into next Tuesday's budget.

Long dated Australian bond yields dropped to their lowest level since late February, prompted by shortcovering following an unusally marked move in U.S. debt in Tokyo on comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan said that growth and inflation would slow in late 1997 going into 1998, but the central bank would act if this does not prove the case.

"I'm a bit bemused by the extent of the rally this side of the globe. (Greenspan) hasn't really given a real clue in what he's going to do next," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

The market is now seen maintaining the rally going into next Tuesday's 1997/98 budget, which is expected to be bond-friendly given that some economists are predicting a headline surplus of some A$10 billion, which could see net fixed-income supply drop to zero.

Traders the day's move was probably exaggerated by relatively thin pre-weekend turnover, and due to short positions, put on after Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane's comments on Thursday, being squeezed out.
The RBA governor has ruled out the chances of a further monetary policy easing.

Local debt continued to outpace the U.S. market, despite its strength in Tokyo trading, and further narrowed its margin to Canada, which was undermined by weakness in the Canadian dollar on Thursday. The yield curve flattened again, making a strong test of support at 85 basis points on the 3/10-year spread.
